preamble: Fronting and assibilation of the voiceless palatal stop [c] to the alveolar affricate [ts]. In Standard Modern Greek /k/ is realized as palatal [c] before front vowels; in the Cycladic Islands and formerly in Old Athenian this palatal is pushed forward to [ts] and merges with original /ts/, a dialect feature known as tsitakism (Κυριακή /kiriaˈki/ 'Sunday' > [tsirjaˈtsi]).

examples.note: Tsitakism: the palatal allophone [c] of /k/ before front vowels is fronted to [ts] and merges with original /ts/; the feature was also shared by Old Athenian.

sources: Trudgill, P. (2003). Modern Greek dialects: A preliminary classification. Journal of Greek Linguistics 4: 45–63. https://doi.org/10.1075/jgl.4.04tru
